intro: Weekly success turns raw logs into learning. Zoom out once a week so daily noise stops running your decisions.
buddyTip: Change only one variable after each weekly review — protein consistency, fibre, steps, or dinner timing — not five at once.
mission: Book a 20-minute weekly review slot. Open Progress, then write one change for next week.
why: Daily weight and hunger swing for reasons that have nothing to do with fat change: sodium, carbs, training, hormones, sleep. Weekly review is where patterns become visible and crash resets become unnecessary.
A good week is not a perfect macro average. It is enough honest days, protein and fibre showing up often, training that matches recovery, and a shopping/meal plan that made weekday decisions easier.
Shopping and meal planning belong in the weekly loop because willpower is a bad grocery strategy. Decide once; execute many times.

what.lead: Cover these themes every week — lightly.
points: Weekly review — Progress trends + Foodiary pattern scan
Shopping — protein anchors, fibre sources, staples that fit your budget
Meal planning — a few realistic dinners, not a fantasy menu
Weight — trend across the week; never crown a single morning king
Protein / fibre consistency — how many days hit “good enough,” not perfection
Training — sessions done vs recovery felt
Goals — keep, tweak, or pause one goal for next week

misconceptions.myth: If average calories were high, I must slash hard next week.
misconceptions.truth: Find the cause: under-logged days, weekend clustering, low protein hunger. Fix the cause; avoid panic deficits.

misconceptions.myth: Meal planning means cooking every lunch.
misconceptions.truth: Planning can mean two repeat dinners, a default lunch, and a restaurant rule. Simplicity scales.

how.lead: Use the same Sunday (or midweek) script so review stays short.
steps: Open Progress for the week — note direction of weight and protein adherence
Scan Foodiary: which meals were missing, which days felt easy
Ask: what did good days share? (protein breakfast, packed lunch, earlier dinner)
Write a short shop list from next week’s meal plan — favour repeatable proteins and fibre
Schedule training that fits sleep, not the other way around
Set one weekly goal sentence; celebrate adherence before criticising averages
how.buddyHelps: Progress shows trends Foodiary cannot shout about daily. Meal Plan holds intent; Home remains where actual intake is logged when you eat.

sections.title: Weight without drama
paras: Compare week averages or multi-day trends. One heavy morning after a salty dinner is information about water, not a moral failure.
If the trend stalls for several weeks with honest logs, adjust energy or activity thoughtfully — still one variable at a time.

sections.title: Protein, fibre, training
paras: Count consistency: days with a clear protein anchor and fibre-containing plants beat chasing a perfect gram total on two heroic days.
Training success includes recovery. A missed session after poor sleep can be wise — log the reality and adjust the plan.

mistakes.quote: I had one bad weekend, so I’m doing a juice cleanse to compensate.
mistakes.why: Compensation extremes teach binge–restrict cycles. Return to the normal weekly plan.

mistakes.quote: I’ll plan fourteen unique gourmet dinners.
mistakes.why: Over-planning collapses by Wednesday. Three reliable dinners beat seven abandoned ones.

mistakes.quote: Weekly review is just looking at the scale.
mistakes.why: Scale without Foodiary context misleads. Pair weight with intake honesty, protein, and life events.

encouragement: A calm weekly review is how amateurs become consistent. Protect the slot — your future self spends less time guessing.
